append.text: **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:2a) *Dómine, audívi auditiónem tuam* → *Senhor, eu ouvi a vossa notícia*** — the row applied; *tuam* left open (report from God / about God). The v1 stylist heard *notícia* as a newspaper word and asked *anúncio*; refused (*anúncio* is the classifieds' word and leans to God as speaker). The CNBB LH has *vossa mensagem*, MS1932 *a tua palavra*, DM1962 *o teu oráculo*; options in `ps225` decision `auditio`. *Eu* supplied: after the vocative, *Senhor, ouvi* is the *vós* imperative.

**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:2b) *opus tuum … vivífica illud* → *a vossa obra … vivificai-a*** — the row, with the resumptive *illud* as the enclitic. The v1 stylist heard *vi-vi-fi-cai-a* as a stumble and asked *dai-lhe vida* (the row's option); held for the concord, option.
**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:2c) *notum fácies* → *a fareis conhecer*** (object *a* = the work, supplied); no reader remarked. The CNBB LH's *tornai-a conhecida* is an option.

**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:4a) *córnua in mánibus ejus* → *chifres nas suas mãos*** — the concrete image against *raios* (MS1932, DM1962, CNBB LH: the Hebrew's sense). Passed the Latinist twice; the ambiguity reader heard literal horns and was puzzled.
**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:5a) *egrediétur diábolus ante pedes ejus* → *o diabo sairá diante dos seus pés*** — the row applied (MS1932 *o demônio* option). The ambiguity reader heard Satan.

**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:6a, 3:11) *Stetit, et mensus est terram* → *Deteve-se, e mediu a terra*; *Sol, et luna stetérunt* → *detiveram-se*** — one verb for the canticle's two *stare*. Draft 1 had *Pôs-se de pé* (81:1); the v1 stylist heard *pés. * Pôs-se de pé* as a pun.

**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:19a) *ponet pedes meos quasi cervórum* → *fará os meus pés como os das corças*** — copied from 17:34 (the same phrase). Both Latinist runs (minor) and the v1 stylist asked *dos cervos* (the Latin's gender); held for the 17:34 homophone evidence, option in `ps225` decision `ponet`.
**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:10b) *Dedit abýssus vocem suam* → *O abismo fez ouvir a sua voz*** — the row applied. Both Latinist runs (minor) asked *deu a sua voz*; refused, as at 45:7 and 76:18.

**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:18) *Ego autem in Dómino gaudébo: et exsultábo* → *Eu, porém, me regozijarei no Senhor: * e exultarei*** — kept apart from exsultáre in the same verse; no reader remarked. The CNBB LH has *me alegro*.

**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:7) *turbabúntur pelles terræ Mádian* → *serão perturbadas as peles da terra de Madiã*** — the tent-skins, parallel to *tentória*; not explained (*pavilhões* MS1932, *tendas de peles* options). The ambiguity reader did not hear the tents.

**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:9a) *Súscitans suscitábis arcum tuum* → *Levantando, levantareis o vosso arco*** — the Latin's doubling kept (rule 2); *Certamente levantareis* (DRB) option. Passed the Latinist twice; the ambiguity reader heard 'an odd repetition'.
**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:12) *In frémitu conculcábis terram* → *No bramido calcareis aos pés a terra*** — the noun of the row's verb; the ambiguity reader listed *bramido* as unknown.
**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:3a) *Deus ab Austro véniet* → *Deus virá do sul***; no reader remarked.
**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:13a) *in salútem cum Christo tuo* → *para a salvação com o vosso Cristo*** (D19; the CNBB LH has *o vosso Ungido*). The ambiguity reader heard Jesus Christ.
**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:19b) *super excélsa mea* → *sobre as minhas alturas*** (D42; *mea* kept).
**Canticle 225 (Hab 3:19a) *ponet pedes meos quasi cervórum* → *fará os meus pés como os das corças*** (82:14 *fazei … como*); no reader remarked on the verb.

terms: | sǽculi (genitive of age: *montes sǽculi*) | dos séculos (*e foram quebrados os montes dos séculos*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:6b)**. Draft 1 *seculares* (MS1932) was heard as 'lay' by the v1 stylist and the ambiguity reader. The v2 Latinist (minor) asked the singular *do século*; refused (heard as 'of the century'). 142:3b *mórtui sǽculi → os mortos de outrora* is a different case (the dead of old). |

| quadríga | quadriga (*e as vossas quadrigas são salvação*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:8b)**; the Latin's specific word, apart from *currus → carros de guerra*. The ambiguity reader listed it as unknown; *carros* is the option. |
| scíndere | fender (*Fendereis os rios da terra*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:9b)**; L&S cleave. MS1932 *dividirás* option. No reader remarked. |

| gurges | redemoinho (*o redemoinho das águas passou*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:9b)**; apart from *abýssus → abismo* (next line) and *turbo → turbilhão* (3:14a). *voragem* (exact, literary) option. |
| turbo (whirlwind) | turbilhão (*que vinham como um turbilhão*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:14a)**; MS1932 *torvelinho*. The CNBB LH uses *turbilhão* for the waters of 3:15. |
| scatére | fervilhar (*e que fervilhe debaixo de mim*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:16b)**; bubbling and swarming (DRB 'swarm'). The ambiguity reader listed it as unknown. |

| putrédo | podridão (*Que a podridão entre nos meus ossos*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:16b)**; the subject put first in draft 2 so *entre* is not heard as 'between' (stylist and ambiguity reader). |
| germen | broto (*e não haverá broto nas vinhas*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:17a)**; *germe* is heard as a germ. |
| denudáre | desnudar (*desnudastes o seu fundamento até o pescoço*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:13b)**; *pusestes a nu* option; MS1932 *descobriste* heard as 'discovered'. |
| obstupefácere | espantar (*e no furor espantareis as nações*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:12)**; MS1932. *deixar atônito* option. |

| fulgúrans | fulgurante (*da vossa lança fulgurante*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:11)**; MS1932; *relampejante* (the *fulgur → relâmpago* family) option. The ambiguity reader listed it as unknown. |

| mentíri (of a crop: *mentiétur opus olívæ*) | mentir (*Mentirá a obra da oliveira*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:17b)**; the Latin's image kept, and *opus → obra* as in 3:2b. DRB 'shall fail', MS1932 *faltará*. The ambiguity reader guessed the failure. |

| Jesus (*in Deo Jesu meo*) | meu Jesus (*e exultarei em Deus, meu Jesus*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:18)**. Jerome's *Jesu* where the Hebrew is 'my salvation' (MS1932, DM1962, the CNBB LH: *meu Salvador*). Rule 1: the Latin's word. Passed the Latinist twice. |

| Deus Dóminus (subject: *Deus Dóminus fortitúdo mea*) | Deus, o Senhor (*Deus, o Senhor, é a minha força*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:19a)**; the Latin's order, *é* supplied. Not 117:27a's sentence *Deus Dóminus → o Senhor é Deus*. *O Senhor Deus* (MS1932) option. |

| abscíndere (a flock from the fold) | cortar (*O rebanho será cortado do aprisco*) | open | **Canticle 225 (Hab 3:17c)**. The v1 stylist asked *arrancado*; refused (*arrancar* is erípere / éruere / evéllere's). |
